title: How much oil can cushion another Middle East supply shock?
gist: Global oil inventories hit 3.35 billion barrels in October, the lowest since January 2017 per Kpler, as the Iran war and Hormuz disruption drain the supply cushion. Aramco's CEO says nearly 3 billion barrels of supply have been lost since late February.

insights.claim: Global oil inventories stood at 3.35 billion barrels in October, the lowest level on record since January 2017, according to Kpler.
insights.so_what: Low buffers amplify price sensitivity to any further supply shock.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton

insights.claim: A brief recovery in Middle Eastern oil exports last month has faltered amid renewed attacks, complicating efforts to rebuild stocks.
insights.so_what: Stock rebuilding is delayed, keeping the market vulnerable and prices supported.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton

insights.claim: Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said on Oct. 5 that the world has lost nearly 3 billion barrels of gross oil supply since the conflict began in late February, roughly half the crude and products that would normally transit Hormuz in that period.
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale of the Hormuz shortfall that inventories have been absorbing.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton

insights.claim: Nasser warned the supply resilience cushion is thin and the system is straining, with little else the world can turn to.
insights.so_what: Producer-side warning that spare capacity and stocks are exhausted; bullish skew for oil risk.
insights.quote: "the supply resilience cushion is scarily thin."
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton
